passages.text: When Samuel died, all Israel gathered to mourn for him; and they buried him at his home in Ramah. Then David set out and went down to the Wilderness of Paran.
passages.sermon:
Samuel was a prophet and leader in Israel.
Samuel died.
All Israel gathered together.
The people mourned for Samuel.
They buried Samuel at his home in Ramah.
David was also in Israel.
After Samuel died, David got up.
David went down to the Wilderness of Paran.
passages.original: וַיָּ֣מָת שְׁמוּאֵ֔ל וַיִּקָּבְצ֤וּ כָל־ יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ וַיִּסְפְּדוּ־ ל֔וֹ וַיִּקְבְּרֻ֥הוּ בְּבֵית֖וֹ בָּרָמָ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם דָּוִ֔ד וַיֵּ֖רֶד אֶל־ מִדְבַּ֥ר פָּארָֽן׃ס

passages.text: Now there was a man in Maon whose business was in Carmel. He was a very wealthy man with a thousand goats and three thousand sheep, which he was shearing in Carmel.
passages.sermon:
There was a man who lived in Maon.
He did his business in Carmel.
This man was very wealthy.
He owned three thousand sheep.
He owned one thousand goats.
He was shearing his sheep in Carmel.
passages.original: וְאִ֨ישׁ בְּמָע֜וֹן וּמַעֲשֵׂ֣הוּ בַכַּרְמֶ֗ל וְהָאִישׁ֙ גָּד֣וֹל מְאֹ֔ד וְל֛וֹ צֹ֥אן שְׁלֹֽשֶׁת־ אֲלָפִ֖ים וְאֶ֣לֶף עִזִּ֑ים וַיְהִ֛י בִּגְזֹ֥ז אֶת־ צֹאנ֖וֹ בַּכַּרְמֶֽל׃

passages.text: His name was Nabal, and his wife’s name was Abigail. She was an intelligent and beautiful woman, but her husband, a Calebite, was harsh and evil in his dealings.
passages.sermon:
There was a man named Nabal.
Nabal lived in Maon.
Nabal was a Calebite.
Nabal had a wife named Abigail.
Abigail was intelligent.
Abigail was beautiful.
Nabal was harsh.
Nabal acted in evil ways.
passages.original: וְשֵׁ֤ם הָאִישׁ֙ נָבָ֔ל וְשֵׁ֥ם אִשְׁתּ֖וֹ אֲבִגָ֑יִל וְהָאִשָּׁ֤ה טֽוֹבַת־ שֶׂ֙כֶל֙ וִ֣יפַת תֹּ֔אַר וְהָאִ֥ישׁ קָשֶׁ֛ה וְרַ֥ע מַעֲלָלִ֖ים וְה֥וּא כְלִבּוֹ׃

passages.text: While David was in the wilderness, he heard that Nabal was shearing sheep.
passages.sermon: David was in the wilderness.\r\nDavid heard news there.\r\nNabal was shearing his sheep.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע דָּוִ֖ד בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר כִּֽי־ גֹזֵ֥ז נָבָ֖ל אֶת־ צֹאנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: So David sent ten young men and instructed them, “Go up to Nabal at Carmel. Greet him in my name and say to him, ‘Long life to you, and peace to you and your house and to all that belongs to you.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader in Israel.
David sent ten young men.
David spoke to these young men.
He gave them instructions.
He told them, "Go up to Carmel."
He said, "Go to Nabal."
He said, "Greet Nabal in my name."
He told them, "Ask Nabal for peace in my name."
He told them what to say.
He said, "Say this to Nabal."
He said, "May you live a long life."
He said, "May you have peace."
He said, "May your house have peace."
He said, "May everything you have have peace."
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד עֲשָׂרָ֣ה נְעָרִ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לַנְּעָרִ֗ים עֲל֤וּ כַרְמֶ֙לָה֙ וּבָאתֶ֣ם אֶל־ נָבָ֔ל וּשְׁאֶלְתֶּם־ ל֥וֹ בִשְׁמִ֖י לְשָׁלֽוֹם׃ וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֥ם כֹּ֖ה לֶחָ֑י וְאַתָּ֤ה שָׁלוֹם֙ וּבֵיתְךָ֣ שָׁל֔וֹם וְכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־ לְךָ֖ שָׁלֽוֹם׃

passages.text: Now I hear that it is time for shearing. When your shepherds were with us, we did not harass them, and nothing of theirs was missing the whole time they were in Carmel.
passages.sermon:
David was in the wilderness.
David heard that Nabal was shearing his sheep.
David spoke to Nabal through his messengers.
David said, “Now I hear it is time for shearing.
Your shepherds were with us.
We did not mistreat them.
We did not harm them.
Nothing was missing from them.
This was true the whole time they were in Carmel.”
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה שָׁמַ֔עְתִּי כִּ֥י גֹזְזִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ עַתָּ֗ה הָרֹעִ֤ים אֲשֶׁר־ לְךָ֙ הָי֣וּ עִמָּ֔נוּ לֹ֣א הֶכְלַמְנ֗וּם וְלֹֽא־ נִפְקַ֤ד לָהֶם֙ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל־ יְמֵ֖י הֱיוֹתָ֥ם בַּכַּרְמֶֽל׃

passages.text: Ask your young men, and they will tell you. So let my young men find favor with you, for we have come on the day of a feast. Please give whatever you can afford to your servants and to your son David.’ ”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Nabal through his messengers.
David asked Nabal to check with his own young men.
David said, "Ask your young men."
"They will tell you the truth."
David wanted Nabal to know his men had acted well.
David said, "Let my young men find favor with you."
David explained, "We have come on a day of celebration."
David requested, "Please give whatever you can to your servants."
David also asked, "Please give to your son David."
passages.original: שְׁאַ֨ל אֶת־ נְעָרֶ֜יךָ וְיַגִּ֣ידוּ לָ֗ךְ וְיִמְצְא֨וּ הַנְּעָרִ֥ים חֵן֙ בְּעֵינֶ֔יךָ כִּֽי־ עַל־ י֥וֹם ט֖וֹב בָּ֑נוּ תְּנָה־ נָּ֗א אֵת֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֤א יָֽדְךָ֙ לַעֲבָדֶ֔יךָ וּלְבִנְךָ֖ לְדָוִֽד׃

passages.text: When David’s young men arrived, they relayed all these words to Nabal on behalf of David. Then they waited.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader in Israel.
David sent young men to Nabal.
The young men arrived at Nabal’s place.
They spoke to Nabal.
They spoke all the words David told them.
They spoke in David’s name.
After they finished speaking, they waited.
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֙אוּ֙ נַעֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַיְדַבְּר֧וּ אֶל־ נָבָ֛ל כְּכָל־ הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵ֖לֶּה בְּשֵׁ֣ם דָּוִ֑ד וַיָּנֽוּחוּ׃

passages.text: But Nabal asked them, “Who is David? Who is this son of Jesse? Many servants these days are breaking away from their masters.
passages.sermon:
Nabal spoke to David’s servants.
Nabal said, “Who is David?
Who is the son of Jesse?
Many servants are running away from their masters these days.”
passages.original: וַיַּ֨עַן נָבָ֜ל אֶת־ עַבְדֵ֤י דָוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר מִ֥י דָוִ֖ד וּמִ֣י בֶן־ יִשָׁ֑י הַיּוֹם֙ רַבּ֣וּ עֲבָדִ֔ים הַמִּתְפָּ֣רְצִ֔ים אִ֖ישׁ מִפְּנֵ֥י אֲדֹנָֽיו׃

passages.text: Why should I take my bread and water and the meat I have slaughtered for my shearers, and give them to these men whose origin I do not know?”
passages.sermon:
Nabal was a wealthy man.
Nabal owned many sheep.
Nabal was harsh and selfish.
Nabal spoke to David’s messengers.
Nabal said, “I have bread.
I have water.
I have meat.
I killed this meat for my shearers.
Should I give my food to men I do not know?
I do not know where these men come from.”
passages.original: וְלָקַחְתִּ֤י אֶת־ לַחְמִי֙ וְאֶת־ מֵימַ֔י וְאֵת֙ טִבְחָתִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר טָבַ֖חְתִּי לְגֹֽזְזָ֑י וְנָֽתַתִּי֙ לַֽאֲנָשִׁ֔ים אֲשֶׁר֙ לֹ֣א יָדַ֔עְתִּי אֵ֥י מִזֶּ֖ה הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: So David’s men turned around and went back, and they relayed to him all these words.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader.
David had young men who served him.
Nabal insulted David’s men and refused their request.
David’s men turned around.
They went back to David.
They told David everything that happened.
They repeated all of Nabal’s words to David.
passages.original: וַיַּהַפְכ֥וּ נַעֲרֵֽי־ דָוִ֖ד לְדַרְכָּ֑ם וַיָּשֻׁ֙בוּ֙ וַיָּבֹ֔אוּ וַיַּגִּ֣דוּ ל֔וֹ כְּכֹ֖ל הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃

passages.text: And David said to his men, “Strap on your swords!” So David and all his men put on their swords, and about four hundred men followed David, while two hundred stayed with the supplies.
passages.sermon:
David was the leader of his men.
David spoke to his men.
David said, “Strap on your swords.”
Each man put on his sword.
David also put on his sword.
About four hundred men followed David.
Two hundred men stayed with the supplies.
passages.original: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ דָּוִ֨ד לַאֲנָשָׁ֜יו חִגְר֣וּ׀ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ חַרְבּ֗וֹ וַֽיַּחְגְּרוּ֙ אִ֣ישׁ אֶת־ חַרְבּ֔וֹ וַיַּחְגֹּ֥ר גַּם־ דָּוִ֖ד אֶת־ חַרְבּ֑וֹ וַֽיַּעֲל֣וּ׀ אַחֲרֵ֣י דָוִ֗ד כְּאַרְבַּ֤ע מֵאוֹת֙ אִ֔ישׁ וּמָאתַ֖יִם יָשְׁב֥וּ עַל־ הַכֵּלִֽים׃

passages.text: Meanwhile, one of Nabal’s young men informed Nabal’s wife Abigail, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness to greet our master, but he scolded them.
passages.sermon:
Abigail was Nabal’s wife.
One of Nabal’s young men spoke to Abigail.
He said, “Look, David sent messengers from the wilderness.
David wanted to greet our master.
But our master scolded them.”
passages.original: וְלַאֲבִיגַ֙יִל֙ אֵ֣שֶׁת נָבָ֔ל הִגִּ֧יד נַֽעַר־ אֶחָ֛ד מֵהַנְּעָרִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר הִנֵּ֣ה שָׁלַח֩ דָּוִ֨ד מַלְאָכִ֧ים׀ מֵֽהַמִּדְבָּ֛ר לְבָרֵ֥ךְ אֶת־ אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וַיָּ֥עַט בָּהֶֽם׃

passages.text: Yet these men were very good to us. When we were in the field, we were not harassed, and nothing of ours went missing the whole time we lived among them.
passages.sermon:
David and his men were with us in the field.
They treated us very well.
They did not harm us.
No one took anything from us.
Nothing of ours went missing the whole time we were with them.
passages.original: וְהָ֣אֲנָשִׁ֔ים טֹבִ֥ים לָ֖נוּ מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹ֤א הָכְלַ֙מְנוּ֙ וְלֹֽא־ פָקַ֣דְנוּ מְא֔וּמָה כָּל־ יְמֵי֙ הִתְהַלַּ֣כְנוּ אִתָּ֔ם בִּֽהְיוֹתֵ֖נוּ בַּשָּׂדֶֽה׃

passages.text: They were a wall around us, both day and night, the whole time we were herding our sheep near them.
passages.sermon:
David and his men protected us.
They stayed with us while we watched our sheep.
They kept us safe every day.
They guarded us every night.
They were like a wall around us the whole time.
passages.original: חוֹמָה֙ הָי֣וּ עָלֵ֔ינוּ גַּם־ לַ֖יְלָה גַּם־ יוֹמָ֑ם כָּל־ יְמֵ֛י הֱיוֹתֵ֥נוּ עִמָּ֖ם רֹעִ֥ים הַצֹּֽאן׃

passages.text: Now consider carefully what you must do, because disaster looms over our master and all his household. For he is such a scoundrel that nobody can speak to him!”
passages.sermon:
Abigail, you must think carefully now.
You must see what you should do.
Disaster is coming to our master and to his whole house.
Our master is a wicked man.
No one can talk to him.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֗ה דְּעִ֤י וּרְאִי֙ מַֽה־ תַּעֲשִׂ֔י כִּֽי־ כָלְתָ֧ה הָרָעָ֛ה אֶל־ אֲדֹנֵ֖ינוּ וְעַ֣ל כָּל־ בֵּית֑וֹ וְהוּא֙ בֶּן־ בְּלִיַּ֔עַל מִדַּבֵּ֖ר אֵלָֽיו׃

passages.text: Then Abigail hurried and took two hundred loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five butchered sheep, five seahs of roasted grain, a hundred clusters of raisins, and two hundred cakes of figs. She loaded them on donkeys and said to her young men, “Go ahead of me. I will be right behind you.” But she did not tell her husband Nabal.
passages.sermon:
Abigail acted quickly.
She took two hundred loaves of bread.
She took two skins of wine.
She took five butchered sheep.
She took five seahs of roasted grain.
She took one hundred clusters of raisins.
She took two hundred cakes of figs.
She put all these things on donkeys.
She spoke to her young men.
She said, “Go ahead of me.
I will come right after you.”
She did not tell her husband Nabal.
passages.original: וַתְּמַהֵ֣ר אֲבוֹגַיִל וַתִּקַּח֩ מָאתַ֨יִם לֶ֜חֶם וּשְׁנַ֣יִם נִבְלֵי־ יַ֗יִן וְחָמֵ֨שׁ צֹ֤אן עֲשָׂווֹת וְחָמֵ֤שׁ סְאִים֙ קָלִ֔י וּמֵאָ֥ה צִמֻּקִ֖ים וּמָאתַ֣יִם דְּבֵלִ֑ים וַתָּ֖שֶׂם עַל־ הַחֲמֹרִֽים׃ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר לִנְעָרֶ֙יהָ֙ עִבְר֣וּ לְפָנַ֔י הִנְנִ֖י אַחֲרֵיכֶ֣ם בָּאָ֑ה וּלְאִישָׁ֥הּ נָבָ֖ל לֹ֥א הִגִּֽידָה׃

passages.text: As Abigail came riding her donkey into a mountain ravine, she saw David and his men coming down toward her, and she met them.
passages.sermon:
Abigail rode her donkey.
She went down into a hidden part of the mountain.
David and his men were coming down toward her.
Abigail met David and his men.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֞ה הִ֣יא׀ רֹכֶ֣בֶת עַֽל־ הַחֲמ֗וֹר וְיֹרֶ֙דֶת֙ בְּסֵ֣תֶר הָהָ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֤ה דָוִד֙ וַאֲנָשָׁ֔יו יֹרְדִ֖ים לִקְרָאתָ֑הּ וַתִּפְגֹּ֖שׁ אֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: Now David had just finished saying, “In vain I have protected all that belonged to this man in the wilderness. Nothing that belongs to him has gone missing, yet he has paid me back evil for good.
passages.sermon:
David was a leader and a protector.
\r\nDavid spoke about his actions.
\r\nDavid said he had guarded everything that belonged to Nabal.
\r\nDavid did this while he was in the wilderness.
\r\nNothing that belonged to Nabal was lost.
\r\nDavid received evil in return for the good he had done.
\r\nNabal paid David back with harm instead of kindness.
passages.original: וְדָוִ֣ד אָמַ֗ר אַךְ֩ לַשֶּׁ֨קֶר שָׁמַ֜רְתִּי אֶֽת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁ֤ר לָזֶה֙ בַּמִּדְבָּ֔ר וְלֹא־ נִפְקַ֥ד מִכָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֖וֹ מְא֑וּמָה וַיָּֽשֶׁב־ לִ֥י רָעָ֖ה תַּ֥חַת טוֹבָֽה׃

passages.text: May God punish David, and ever so severely, if I let one of Nabal’s men survive until morning.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke.
\r\nDavid was angry at Nabal.
\r\nDavid made a vow.
\r\nDavid said, “May God punish my enemies.
\r\nMay God punish them severely.
\r\nIf I let even one of Nabal’s men live until morning, may God do this to me.
\r\nI will not leave a single man alive who belongs to Nabal.”
passages.original: כֹּה־ יַעֲשֶׂ֧ה אֱלֹהִ֛ים לְאֹיְבֵ֥י דָוִ֖ד וְכֹ֣ה יֹסִ֑יף אִם־ אַשְׁאִ֧יר מִכָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ ל֛וֹ עַד־ הַבֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּקִֽיר׃

passages.text: When Abigail saw David, she quickly got off the donkey, fell facedown, and bowed before him.
passages.sermon:
Abigail was the wife of Nabal.
David was a leader and a warrior.
Abigail saw David.
She acted quickly.
She got down from the donkey.
She fell on her face before David.
She bowed to the ground.
passages.original: וַתֵּ֤רֶא אֲבִיגַ֙יִל֙ אֶת־ דָּוִ֔ד וַתְּמַהֵ֕ר וַתֵּ֖רֶד מֵעַ֣ל הַחֲמ֑וֹר וַתִּפֹּ֞ל לְאַפֵּ֤י דָוִד֙ עַל־ פָּנֶ֔יהָ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ אָֽרֶץ׃

passages.text: She fell at his feet and said, “My lord, may the blame be on me alone, but please let your servant speak to you; hear the words of your servant.
passages.sermon:
Abigail fell at David’s feet.
She spoke to David.
She said, “My lord, let the blame fall on me alone.
Please let your servant speak to you.
Please listen to the words of your servant.”
passages.original: וַתִּפֹּל֙ עַל־ רַגְלָ֔יו וַתֹּ֕אמֶר בִּי־ אֲנִ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י הֶֽעָוֺ֑ן וּֽתְדַבֶּר־ נָ֤א אֲמָֽתְךָ֙ בְּאָזְנֶ֔יךָ וּשְׁמַ֕ע אֵ֖ת דִּבְרֵ֥י אֲמָתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: My lord should pay no attention to this scoundrel Nabal, for he lives up to his name: His name means Fool, and folly accompanies him. I, your servant, did not see my lord’s young men whom you sent.
passages.sermon:
Abigail spoke to David.
Abigail said, "My lord, do not pay attention to this wicked man Nabal."
Nabal is a fool.
His name means Fool.
Foolishness is with him.
I am your servant.
I did not see the young men you sent."
passages.original: אַל־ נָ֣א יָשִׂ֣ים אֲדֹנִ֣י׀ אֶת־ לִבּ֡וֹ אֶל־ אִישׁ֩ הַבְּלִיַּ֨עַל הַזֶּ֜ה עַל־ נָבָ֗ל כִּ֤י כִשְׁמוֹ֙ כֶּן־ ה֔וּא נָבָ֣ל שְׁמ֔וֹ וּנְבָלָ֖ה עִמּ֑וֹ וַֽאֲנִי֙ אֲמָ֣תְךָ֔ לֹ֥א רָאִ֛יתִי אֶת־ נַעֲרֵ֥י אֲדֹנִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר שָׁלָֽחְתָּ׃

passages.text: Now, my lord, as surely as the LORD lives and you yourself live, the LORD has held you back from coming to bloodshed and avenging yourself with your own hand. May your enemies and those who seek harm for my lord be like Nabal.
passages.sermon:
Abigail spoke to David.
Abigail called David "my lord."
Abigail said, "As surely as the LORD lives."
Abigail said, "As surely as you live."
The LORD stopped you, David, from shedding blood.
The LORD kept you from taking revenge with your own hand.
May your enemies be like Nabal.
May those who seek to harm you become like Nabal.
passages.original: וְעַתָּ֣ה אֲדֹנִ֗י חַי־ יְהוָ֤ה וְחֵֽי־ נַפְשְׁךָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר מְנָעֲךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ מִבּ֣וֹא בְדָמִ֔ים וְהוֹשֵׁ֥עַ יָדְךָ֖ לָ֑ךְ וְעַתָּ֗ה יִֽהְי֤וּ כְנָבָל֙ אֹיְבֶ֔יךָ וְהַֽמְבַקְשִׁ֥ים אֶל־ אֲדֹנִ֖י רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: Now let this gift your servant has brought to my lord be given to the young men who follow you.
passages.sermon:
Abigail is speaking to David.
Abigail is a servant.
David is her lord.
Abigail has brought a gift to David.
Abigail asks David to accept this gift.
Abigail wants the gift to be given to the young men.
These young men follow David.
Abigail asks that the young men receive the gift.
passages.original: וְעַתָּה֙ הַבְּרָכָ֣ה הַזֹּ֔את אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֥יא שִׁפְחָתְךָ֖ לַֽאדֹנִ֑י וְנִתְּנָה֙ לַנְּעָרִ֔ים הַמִּֽתְהַלְּכִ֖ים בְּרַגְלֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: Please forgive your servant’s offense, for the LORD will surely make a lasting dynasty for my lord, because he fights the LORD’s battles. May no evil be found in you as long as you live.
passages.sermon:
Abigail spoke to David.
Abigail asked David to forgive her offense.
Abigail called herself his servant.
Abigail said the LORD will surely make a lasting house for David.
Abigail said the LORD will do this for David because David fights the LORD’s battles.
Abigail prayed that no evil would be found in David as long as he lives.
passages.original: שָׂ֥א נָ֖א לְפֶ֣שַׁע אֲמָתֶ֑ךָ כִּ֣י עָשֹֽׂה־ יַעֲשֶׂה֩ יְהוָ֨ה לַֽאדֹנִ֜י בַּ֣יִת נֶאֱמָ֗ן כִּי־ מִלְחֲמ֤וֹת יְהוָה֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י נִלְחָ֔ם וְרָעָ֛ה לֹא־ תִמָּצֵ֥א בְךָ֖ מִיָּמֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: And should someone pursue you and seek your life, then the life of my lord will be bound securely by the LORD your God in the bundle of the living. But He shall fling away the lives of your enemies like stones from a sling.
passages.sermon:
David was a servant of the LORD God.
Sometimes, a person may rise up to chase you.
Someone may try to take your life.
But the LORD your God will protect your life.
He will keep your life safe among the living.
He will hold your life securely.
The LORD will deal with your enemies.
He will throw away their lives like stones from a sling.
passages.original: וַיָּ֤קָם אָדָם֙ לִרְדָפְךָ֔ וּלְבַקֵּ֖שׁ אֶת־ נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ וְֽהָיְתָה֩ נֶ֨פֶשׁ אֲדֹנִ֜י צְרוּרָ֣ה׀ בִּצְר֣וֹר הַחַיִּ֗ים אֵ֚ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ וְאֵ֨ת נֶ֤פֶשׁ אֹיְבֶ֙יךָ֙ יְקַלְּעֶ֔נָּה בְּת֖וֹךְ כַּ֥ף הַקָּֽלַע׃

passages.text: When the LORD has done for my lord all the good He promised, and when He has appointed you ruler over Israel, then my lord will have no remorse or guilt of conscience over needless bloodshed and revenge. And when the LORD has dealt well with my lord, may you remember your maidservant.”
passages.sermon:
The LORD made promises to you, my lord.
The LORD will do all the good things He spoke about you.
The LORD will appoint you as ruler over Israel.
You, my lord, will not have regret.
You will not have guilt in your heart.
You will not be troubled by shedding blood without cause.
You will not be troubled by taking revenge for yourself.
The LORD will do good to you, my lord.
Please remember me, your servant.
passages.original: וְהָיָ֗ה כִּֽי־ יַעֲשֶׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י כְּכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ דִּבֶּ֥ר אֶת־ הַטּוֹבָ֖ה עָלֶ֑יךָ וְצִוְּךָ֥ לְנָגִ֖יד עַל־ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ וְלֹ֣א תִהְיֶ֣ה זֹ֣את׀ לְךָ֡ לְפוּקָה֩ וּלְמִכְשׁ֨וֹל לֵ֜ב לַאדֹנִ֗י וְלִשְׁפָּךְ־ דָּם֙ חִנָּ֔ם וּלְהוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אֲדֹנִ֖י ל֑וֹ וְהֵיטִ֤ב יְהוָה֙ לַֽאדֹנִ֔י וְזָכַרְתָּ֖ אֶת־ אֲמָתֶֽךָ׃ס

passages.text: Then David said to Abigail, “Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, who sent you to meet me this day!
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abigail.
David was a future king of Israel.
Abigail was the wife of Nabal.
David said, “Blessed is the LORD.
The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD sent you to meet me today.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר דָּוִ֖ד לַאֲבִיגַ֑ל בָּר֤וּךְ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֧ר שְׁלָחֵ֛ךְ הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה לִקְרָאתִֽי׃

passages.text: Blessed is your discernment, and blessed are you, because today you kept me from bloodshed and from avenging myself by my own hand.
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abigail.
David praised Abigail’s wisdom.
David said, “Your discernment is blessed.”
David said, “You are blessed.”
David explained why he blessed her.
David said, “Today you kept me from shedding blood.”
David said, “Today you kept me from taking revenge by my own hand.”
passages.original: וּבָר֥וּךְ טַעְמֵ֖ךְ וּבְרוּכָ֣ה אָ֑תְּ אֲשֶׁ֨ר כְּלִתִ֜נִי הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ מִבּ֣וֹא בְדָמִ֔ים וְהֹשֵׁ֥עַ יָדִ֖י לִֽי׃

passages.text: Otherwise, as surely as the LORD, the God of Israel, lives, who has restrained me from harming you, if you had not come quickly to meet me, then surely no male belonging to Nabal would have been left alive by morning light.”
passages.sermon:
David spoke to Abigail.
David is the future king of Israel.
Abigail is the wife of Nabal.
David said, “The LORD is the God of Israel.
The LORD lives.
The LORD stopped me from harming you.
If you had not hurried to meet me,
If you had not come quickly,
Then by morning,
No male belonging to Nabal would have remained alive.
passages.original: וְאוּלָ֗ם חַי־ יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר מְנָעַ֔נִי מֵהָרַ֖ע אֹתָ֑ךְ כִּ֣י׀ לוּלֵ֣י מִהַ֗רְתְּ וַתָּבֹאתִי לִקְרָאתִ֔י כִּ֣י אִם־ נוֹתַ֧ר לְנָבָ֛ל עַד־ א֥וֹר הַבֹּ֖קֶר מַשְׁתִּ֥ין בְּקִֽיר׃

passages.text: Then David accepted from her hand what she had brought him, and he said to her, “Go home in peace. See, I have heeded your voice and granted your request.”
passages.sermon:
David was a leader of Israel.
Abigail was the wife of Nabal.
Abigail brought gifts to David.
David took from Abigail’s hand what she brought him.
David spoke to Abigail.
David said, “Go home in peace.”
David said, “I have listened to your voice.”
David said, “I have granted your request.”
passages.original: וַיִּקַּ֤ח דָּוִד֙ מִיָּדָ֔הּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ הֵבִ֖יאָה ל֑וֹ וְלָ֣הּ אָמַ֗ר עֲלִ֤י לְשָׁלוֹם֙ לְבֵיתֵ֔ךְ רְאִי֙ שָׁמַ֣עְתִּי בְקוֹלֵ֔ךְ וָאֶשָּׂ֖א פָּנָֽיִךְ׃

passages.text: When Abigail returned to Nabal, there he was in the house, holding a feast fit for a king, in high spirits and very drunk. So she told him nothing until morning light.
passages.sermon:
Abigail was Nabal’s wife.
Abigail returned to Nabal.
Nabal was in his house.
Nabal was holding a feast.
The feast was like a king’s feast.
Nabal was in high spirits.
Nabal was very drunk.
Abigail did not tell Nabal anything that night.
Abigail did not tell him anything small or great until morning.
passages.original: וַתָּבֹ֣א אֲבִיגַ֣יִל׀ אֶל־ נָבָ֡ל וְהִנֵּה־ לוֹ֩ מִשְׁתֶּ֨ה בְּבֵית֜וֹ כְּמִשְׁתֵּ֣ה הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ וְלֵ֤ב נָבָל֙ ט֣וֹב עָלָ֔יו וְה֥וּא שִׁכֹּ֖ר עַד־ מְאֹ֑ד וְלֹֽא־ הִגִּ֣ידָה לּ֗וֹ דָּבָ֥ר קָטֹ֛ן וְגָד֖וֹל עַד־ א֥וֹר הַבֹּֽקֶר׃

passages.text: In the morning when Nabal was sober, his wife told him about these events, and his heart failed within him and he became like a stone.
passages.sermon:
Nabal was Abigail’s husband.
Nabal had been drunk the night before.
Morning came.
Nabal was now sober.
Abigail spoke to Nabal.
Abigail told Nabal about the events that had happened.
Nabal heard Abigail’s words.
Nabal’s heart failed inside him.
Nabal became like a stone.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י בַבֹּ֗קֶר בְּצֵ֤את הַיַּ֙יִן֙ מִנָּבָ֔ל וַתַּגֶּד־ ל֣וֹ אִשְׁתּ֔וֹ אֶת־ הַדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וַיָּ֤מָת לִבּוֹ֙ בְּקִרְבּ֔וֹ וְה֖וּא הָיָ֥ה לְאָֽבֶן׃

passages.text: About ten days later, the LORD struck Nabal dead.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is the God of Israel.
Nabal was a wealthy man.
About ten days passed.
The LORD struck Nabal.
Nabal died.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֖י כַּעֲשֶׂ֣רֶת הַיָּמִ֑ים וַיִּגֹּ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־ נָבָ֖ל וַיָּמֹֽת׃

passages.text: On hearing that Nabal was dead, David said, “Blessed be the LORD, who has upheld my cause against the reproach of Nabal and has restrained His servant from evil. For the LORD has brought the wickedness of Nabal down upon his own head.” Then David sent word to Abigail, asking for her in marriage.
passages.sermon:
David heard that Nabal was dead.
David spoke.
David said, “Blessed be the LORD.”
The LORD upheld my cause against Nabal’s insult.
The LORD kept His servant from doing evil.
The LORD brought Nabal’s wickedness back on Nabal’s own head.
David sent messengers to Abigail.
David asked Abigail to become his wife.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע דָּוִד֮ כִּ֣י מֵ֣ת נָבָל֒ וַיֹּ֡אמֶר בָּר֣וּךְ יְהוָ֡ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָב֩ אֶת־ רִ֨יב חֶרְפָּתִ֜י מִיַּ֣ד נָבָ֗ל וְאֶת־ עַבְדּוֹ֙ חָשַׂ֣ךְ מֵֽרָעָ֔ה וְאֵת֙ רָעַ֣ת נָבָ֔ל הֵשִׁ֥יב יְהוָ֖ה בְּרֹאשׁ֑וֹ וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח דָּוִד֙ וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר בַּאֲבִיגַ֔יִל לְקַחְתָּ֥הּ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: When his servants came to Abigail at Carmel, they said, “David has sent us to take you as his wife.”
passages.sermon:
David was a leader chosen by God.
David sent his servants to Abigail.
Abigail lived at Carmel.
The servants arrived at Abigail’s home.
The servants spoke to Abigail.
They said, “David has sent us to you.”
They said, “He wants to take you as his wife.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֜אוּ עַבְדֵ֥י דָוִ֛ד אֶל־ אֲבִיגַ֖יִל הַכַּרְמֶ֑לָה וַיְדַבְּר֤וּ אֵלֶ֙יהָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר דָּוִד֙ שְׁלָחָ֣נוּ אֵלַ֔יִךְ לְקַחְתֵּ֥ךְ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: She arose, then bowed facedown and said, “Here is your maidservant, ready to serve and to wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”
passages.sermon:
Abigail was a wise and humble woman.
David sent messengers to Abigail.
They asked her to become David’s wife.
Abigail stood up.
She bowed down with her face to the ground.
She spoke to David’s messengers.
She said, “I am your servant.”
She said, “I am ready to serve.”
She said, “I will wash the feet of my lord’s servants.”
passages.original: וַתָּ֕קָם וַתִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ אַפַּ֖יִם אָ֑רְצָה וַתֹּ֗אמֶר הִנֵּ֤ה אֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לְשִׁפְחָ֔ה לִרְחֹ֕ץ רַגְלֵ֖י עַבְדֵ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי׃

passages.text: So Abigail hurried and got on a donkey, and attended by five of her maidens, she followed David’s messengers and became his wife.
passages.sermon:
Abigail was a woman from Carmel.
David sent messengers to Abigail.
Abigail acted quickly.
She stood up.
She got on a donkey.
Five of her maidens walked beside her.
Abigail followed David’s messengers.
Abigail became David’s wife.
passages.original: וַתְּמַהֵ֞ר וַתָּ֣קָם אֲבִיגַ֗יִל וַתִּרְכַּב֙ עַֽל־ הַחֲמ֔וֹר וְחָמֵשׁ֙ נַעֲרֹתֶ֔יהָ הַהֹלְכ֖וֹת לְרַגְלָ֑הּ וַתֵּ֗לֶךְ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י דָוִ֔ד וַתְּהִי־ ל֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: David had also married Ahinoam of Jezreel. So she and Abigail were both his wives.
passages.sermon:
David married Ahinoam.
Ahinoam came from Jezreel.
David also married Abigail.
Abigail and Ahinoam both became David’s wives.
passages.original: וְאֶת־ אֲחִינֹ֛עַם לָקַ֥ח דָּוִ֖ד מִֽיִּזְרְעֶ֑אל וַתִּהְיֶ֛יןָ גַּֽם־ שְׁתֵּיהֶ֥ן ל֖וֹ לְנָשִֽׁים׃ס

passages.text: But Saul had given his daughter Michal, David’s wife, to Palti son of Laish, who was from Gallim.
passages.sermon:
Saul was the king of Israel.
Michal was Saul’s daughter.
Michal was also David’s wife.
Saul gave Michal to another man.
The man’s name was Palti.
Palti was the son of Laish.
Palti was from Gallim.
passages.original: וְשָׁא֗וּל נָתַ֛ן אֶת־ מִיכַ֥ל בִּתּ֖וֹ אֵ֣שֶׁת דָּוִ֑ד לְפַלְטִ֥י בֶן־ לַ֖יִשׁ אֲשֶׁ֥ר מִגַּלִּֽים׃
